annotation.title_clean: Wearable Four Degree of Freedom Upper-Limb Soft Robotic Rehabilitation Device, Disney Doesn't Care: Analyzing Ethical Failures in the AI Replication of James Earl Jones's Voice Through Care Ethics
annotation.title_en: Wearable Four Degree of Freedom Upper-Limb Soft Robotic Rehabilitation Device, Disney Doesn't Care: Analyzing Ethical Failures in the AI Replication of James Earl Jones's Voice Through Care Ethics
annotation.venue: University of Virginia Libra (Online Archive of University of Virginia Scholarship)
annotation.summary_en: Undergraduate engineering capstone record combining a technical project (wearable four-DOF soft robotic upper-limb exoskeleton for stroke rehabilitation) with an STS paper applying care ethics to Disney's AI replica of James Earl Jones's Darth Vader voice in Fortnite. Only the abstract is available; the full text is restricted.
key_provisions_or_claims: Care ethics is applied to assess company duties toward users and employees.
Disney's use of the AI Vader voice in Fortnite is argued to show lack of care toward SAG-AFTRA and young consumers.
Technical project: lightweight, inexpensive wearable soft exoskeleton for home stroke rehabilitation.
Engineers should design with users in mind and proactively raise safety concerns.
